title: Constrained decoding
brief: Lift a byte-level DFA to a token mask, sample under it, cache it, jump over forced text, and keep one grammar state per batch row.
hints: A token is legal only if all of its bytes keep the DFA alive, not just the first byte.
Apply the mask before top-k. If top-k runs first, the k survivors can all be illegal.
Jump forward only through states that are not accepting. An accepting state can also stop.
One mask per request: rows of a batch are usually in different grammar states.
